summary: Yutaka Kawasaki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seio Okuda. He was an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024) and held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and IIBS (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under Louis Renou, Atsuuji Ashikaga, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986).

Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1972–1999).

Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) specializes in history, archaeology, Japanology, and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University and Kyoto University (2006).

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo and completed a doctorate at Rissho University. He served as an associate professor at Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) was a scholar in sinology and linguistics who studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady. He later taught at Peking University (~1923–1926).

Yuto Kawamura works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held positions at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), Kyoto University (post-doc fellow, 2015–2018), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (associate professor, attested 2026).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) was a sinology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Kyushu University, and Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya. He was a professor at Hitotsubashi University, the University of Tokyo, and Daito Bunka University.

Yün-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University (1953) and served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Zack Beer is a student in Buddhist studies and Indology, attested in 2026 as studying at both the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the University of California, Berkeley.

Zalman Movshevich Dymshits (1921–1990) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University (~1946–1950). He taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1953–1954) and was a professor at MGIMO (from 1954).

Zarawar Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar and served as assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin (~1925–1929) and later studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zayn Kassam works in religious studies and philosophy. At Pomona College, she served as department chair, associate dean, and endowed professor from 1995. She also directed the Pacific Basin Institute and became director of the Institute of Ismaili Studies in 2023.
Zdeněk Materna (1900–1944) was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University, where he studied under Josef Zubatý from around 1919 to 1925.

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., among others, and held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).

Zellig Harris (1909–1992) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at Columbia University and taught at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1934 to 1979.

Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies under Toshinori Ochiai and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji between approximately 1931 and 1934.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of California and trained under Richard Baker, Jōshin Kasai, and Mel Weitsman. She served as co-abbess at the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
